findings.title: E-602 overflows its title block: the NEC 220.82 allowance row prints over the footer, and the LED-run and supply tables truncate names and run into each other

evidence.measured: p175 of permit_set_full.pdf (200 dpi crop): the last row of CONNECTED LIGHTING LOAD ('NEC 220.82 allowance | 4,900 ft2 | 14,700 VA at 3 VA/ft2') sits across the title-block top rule and 'Catlin House'/'PROJECT NO' text. LED RUNS table 1 clips 'ED-B-SAUNA-LT-PSU' past its column and abuts table 2; Run column shows 'LR-B-SAUNA-SC', 'LR-M-KIT-N-WE1', Room 'RM-B-SAU', 'RM-M-LIV'. Luminaire schedule columns Description/Brand/Lamp/Listing/Dim-capable are cut ('Nora Lightin', 'PAR20 LE', 'dam'). Control schedule rows are ~3 px high, unreadable.
evidence.expected: Every cell legible and every table inside the drawing area, clear of the title block (a reviewer cannot confirm lamp, listing or dimmer from a clipped cell).
evidence.method: Read p175 of baseline/permit_set_full.pdf; pdftoppm -f 175 -l 175 -r 200, crop the lower third (scratchpad M3/e602_crop.png).

findings.proposed_fix: Let the E-602 tables paginate (a second sheet) or shrink the font/auto-size columns to content; clip the lower block above the title block.

findings.title: E-101 and E-102 plot the house at 1/16" and 3/32" on a 24x36 sheet: devices and labels overprint into unreadable clusters

evidence.measured: E-101 scale 1/16"=1'-0" and E-102 3/32"=1'-0"; the 36 ft house is ~230-340 px of a 1400 px drawing field (E-103/E-104/E-203 use 3/16" and 1/8"). Panel-wall, kitchen, bath and workshop clusters on E-101/E-102 show tag text stacked over tag text (e.g. 'B-WORKSHOP-LT5/RC1/RC2', 'M-BATH1/BATH2 PSU' blocks). The garage/canopy storey plan share the sheet, which sets the scale.
evidence.expected: Plan scale large enough that each device tag is readable (E-103/E-104 at 3/16" are legible); or split the garage/court onto its own sheet so the house plots at 3/16".
evidence.method: Open permit_set_full.pdf pp166-167; compare with pp168-169 (same generator).

findings.proposed_fix: Plot the house alone at >=3/16" (garage and court as a separate or inset view).

findings.title: ED-A-STUBATH-CAN1 (2-1/4" wafer) sits 2.3" above the finished sloped ceiling it lights through, inside the rafter bay

evidence.measured: Can body z 324.87..327.12" (mount ft(7) off the finished floor at x=165", y=234"). Finished gypsum at that point: roof_height_at 336.53" - roof_underside_depth_m(RM-A-STUBATH) 13.975" = 322.55"; rafter bottom 323.25". So the body floats 2.32" above the ceiling face and its base is 1.6" up inside the TJI bay (the 6-7/8" batt holds it, so no clash). The authoring comment says x=13'-9" is where H(x)=7'-0"; the roof assembly was deepened to 13.28" plumb since.
evidence.expected: Wafer flange on the finished face (322.55") i.e. mount ~ 6'-9 11/16" AFF at x=13'-9"; or re-station x so H(x)=7'-0".
evidence.method: $M3/p17.py: roof_height_at(RF-HOUSE,(165,234)) - roof_underside_depth_m(model, roof, 'RM-A-STUBATH'); compare ED-A-STUBATH-CAN1 canvas body_z0.

findings.source: typehaus.resolve.roof_geometry; CLAUDE.md 'line every attic station answers to' (1 1/2" + x/2 - now 1 1/2" + x/2 minus lining)
findings.proposed_fix: Mount the can at the resolved ceiling plane (derive z from roof_underside_at) or lower the elevation 2.3".

findings.title: Sconces on concrete stand 1.6" farther off the wall than modelled: the footprint ignores the RACO 192 + 753 stand-off under the fixture

evidence.measured: WAC sheet (Nov 2026 revision, line drawing read): body 12 H x 4-1/2 W, backplate 4-1/2 x 4-1/2 x 1 in., 2-1/2 in. overall projection from the mounting plane. The fixture mounts on the cover face 1.5625" off the concrete (resolved projection_m), so true projection from the wall = 1.56 + 2.5 = ~4.1". The device footprint is 2.5" from the wall face and place_box only hulls it with the 1.56" box ring (hull = max 2.5"). The 1" canopy is also shallower than the 1.56-1.63" box+cover, so the box sides show (accepted, field-painted, notes/basement_surface_wiring.md).
evidence.expected: Fixture footprint offset by box projection on surface boxes (approx 4.1" from wall) for clearance, collision and the plan symbol.
evidence.method: $M3/p3.py (box projection) + WAC Roland spec sheet drawing (waclighting.com/product/roland/?download=specs3, p1 line drawing).

findings.source: WAC WS-83212 spec sheet line drawing; houses/catlin/notes/basement_surface_wiring.md
findings.proposed_fix: In place_box, shift a surface-box device body out by projection_m (BoxRow.use=luminaire); no catalog change.

findings.title: RACO 192 box is authored 1-1/2" deep; the RACO sheet it cites says 1.563" (plus a 0.063" 753 cover = 1.626", model 1.5625")

evidence.measured: BoxRow(box_size depth inch(1.5), cover_rise inch(0.0625)) -> projection 1.5625". The row's own comment says 'drawn ... 1.563" deep'. Hubbell 192 sheet: 'Ea Length/Depth (in.): 1.563'; 753 sheet: thickness 0.063 in. Box + cover = 1.626".
evidence.method: pdftotext of hubbellcdn.com/specsheet/192.pdf and RACO-753-SPEC-EN.pdf (read this round).

findings.proposed_fix: Set the BoxRow depth to inch(1.563).

findings.title: 26 nail-on flush boxes sit on a stud, king or jack (full stud width inside the box ring); the resolved model gives no stud-adjacent box station

evidence.measured: Probe $M3/p8.py: ring of every flush box (B122A 2.25 wide, BH235A 4.0) vs studs/kings/jacks (1.5" wide, z-overlap): 39 boxes overlap, 26 by >=1.0 in2 (e.g. LAUNDRY-DR1 on W-M-CLN, LIVING-RC12 on W-M-HS4, BATH2-SW-EVE, STUDY2-SW on a jack: 2.25 in2 = a whole stud inside the box). Round 1 checked only box depth vs cavity. A nail-on B122A bears on a stud's side, so the box must move up to ~1.1-2.6" along the wall.
evidence.expected: Station each box beside a stud (as the 2026-10-03 design log did for KMX1/KGF3), or let the engine snap the box ring to the nearest stud edge and report the move.
evidence.method: $M3/p8.py: shapely ring vs Point(mem.p0).buffer(0.75", square) for stud/king/jack/corner/cripple/trimmer, z-overlap with box.

findings.source: DESIGN-LOG 2026-10-03 (receptacles 'nudged off studs'); Carlon catalog p.4 B122A 3-3/4 L x 2-1/4 W
findings.proposed_fix: Nudge the 26 stations (<=2.6") or add a stud-clash advisory; no model change needed for the build (electrician shifts at rough-in).

findings.title: Fridge/freezer DVFR1W boxes are 2.4"-5.8" off the nearest stud, and the new-work screw mounting needs one; trim stand-off still unpublished

evidence.measured: W-M-C5 studs at y=352, 368, 384" (1.5" wide); KFZ1 box y 355.15..359.35 (2.40" from the 352 stud edge); KRF1 y 374.52..378.72 (4.53" and 5.77" clear of its neighbours). Arlington Q-3 sheet: 4.200 x 6.698 x 3.875 in., 'New Work: screws provided for easy mounting to stud'; no trim thickness is printed. Cavity 5.5" vs 3.875" body: fits; the fridge back stands 0.95" off the wall face (220.2 vs 219.25).
evidence.expected: Box adjacent to a stud (or a 2x blocking pad) so the wings screw home; confirm trim proud dimension against the 0.95" fridge gap.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a 2x4 flat block at each box or move 2.4"/4.5" to a stud; ask Arlington for trim thickness.

findings.title: electrical.wall_device_opening cannot grade the three court-concrete devices: its wall map holds framed walls only (FoundationWall W-SG-W1/E1 are skipped, 3 UNKNOWN)

evidence.measured: baseline checks.json: three UNKNOWN 'attachment wall is unresolved'. model.wall('W-SG-W1') resolves (FoundationWall) but `walls = {wall.tag: wall for wall in ctx.model.walls}` (line 37) does not contain it, so the lookup at line 56 fails. Round-2 baseline 208 UNKNOWN includes these.
evidence.expected: Foundation/retaining walls in the map (or N/A earned: no opening in W-SG-W1/E1 at the device station).

findings.proposed_fix: Fall back to ctx.model.wall(tag) for foundation walls.

findings.title: TODO says 13 wall-light types state no canopy; the check reports 12 types / 29 lights, all on flush B122A boxes

evidence.measured: checks.json: 'UNKNOWN - 29 wall light(s) of 12 type(s) state no canopy'. Probe $M3/p21.py: 12 types (KARLIE-2/3, MIRROR-DAY, HALO, SCONCE-CANDLE/SPOT/STAIR/VANITY, SPOT-SW, WALL-LINEAR) x 29 devices, all mounting 'flush' (2.25 x 3.75 box); none on a surface box; every authored footprint is >= 4.25 wide, so none is likely to leave the 2.25" face bare.
evidence.expected: TODO count 12; note that no unstated canopy sits on a concrete surface box, so the residual risk is only a body narrower than 2.25 x 3.75.
evidence.method: grep the unknown text in baseline/checks.json; $M3/p21.py.

findings.proposed_fix: Correct the TODO count; author canopy on the 12 types when sheets are read.
